narrative:
The model predicts you have a 15% chance of failing your final year, which is low enough that the school requires you to take remedial courses as a precaution.

The decision rests mainly on three aspects of your situation. The most influential factor was your reason for choosing this school: you selected it for its reputation. Among students who passed, far more chose the school for its specific courses rather than reputation, so this choice worked against you. The second strongest influence was that you have had no past class failures. While this is exactly the same as the average for students who passed and might seem positive, in your overall profile the model saw it as not providing the extra push needed to offset other risks. Third, the quality of your family relationships, which you described as good, also pulled the prediction slightly toward failing compared with students who reported even stronger family bonds.

Taken together, these elements led the model to recommend extra support. To improve, you should focus on strengthening your daily study habits beyond the 2–5 hours you currently spend, since most successful students in your group study at least that much or more. Consider talking with your teachers about aligning your work more closely with the course demands rather than relying on the school’s general reputation. Small, consistent changes in these areas can noticeably raise your chances of passing without remediation. (218 words)
